blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're moving on to the sequence for [Baby F] now if the jury want to find that on their iPads, to work those independently of what we're going to be showing on the screens.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mrs Hocknell, welcome back. Could you identify yourself for the sake of the record, please?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Claire Hocknell.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We're moving to the sequence for [Baby E]. In some respects parts of this mirror [Baby F]'s sequence for obvious reasons --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, this is [Baby F]'s sequence.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Sorry, they mirror [Baby E]'s sequence.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I think they dovetail, that's the point.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: You'll appreciate, some of these events were contemporaneous as you would have realised.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, not least tile 1, which is untimed, but if we could just go to what's behind that, please. I don't think we need to go to the original document because we've done this once. You have transcribed part of what appears on the record, haven't you?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Could you take us through what you have transcribed, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Parents: [Parents of Babies E & F]. Antenatal history: High risk Down's screen, 165. Mild polyhydramnios.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: MCDA twin. Type 3. SIUGR with stage 1 TTTS on a background of increasing risk for T21."
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Moving to tile 2, first, the birth of [Baby E], which we've seen already. Secondly, the birth of [Baby F] at tile 3. That is recorded at 17.54. He of course was twin 2.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The gestation of both twins is recorded. [Baby F]'s weight recorded at 1.434 kilograms.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: "Born in good condition, cried at birth"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: You have recorded the fact that Dr Ogden made a note of the Apgar score of 6 at 1 minute, but these scores at 5 and 10 minutes were not recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Tile 4 next, please. Sixteen minutes later, both twins were admitted to the neonatal unit.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 5 next, please. Is this Dr Ogden's notes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Dr Ogden will be coming to give evidence, so I won't deal with those because if I do, we're just going to be replicating everything.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The pertinent fact from this observation you have put on to the tile, haven't you, a very low blood glucose level of 1.9?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 6 -- next, please -- is I think a continuation of Dr Ogden's records --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- at 18.30. So this is 20 minutes after admission into the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at tile 7, you have done one of your summaries, simply saying that from that time, in other words from 6.30 pm onwards on 29 July, [Baby F] continued to receive care in the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And so far as the date of the birthday is concerned, those are the records that feature in the sequence?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We move next to tile 8, please. Does that record that [Baby F] was extubated, so an ET tube removed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I'm just querying the date on that slide though.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I think that that should be 30 July.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Okay, yes. We'll just mark that up for a correction.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 9 is a blood gas chart; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We'll go to this because it's annotated by Ailsa Simpson, who's not a witness. This follows the format that the jury have seen many times in this case of a blood gas record and here we see that by 21.57 on 30 July, so it's the entry just by the lower of what would be the holes in the page, that black dot
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: to the left-hand side of the page, we understand now it's a capillary sample. We can see that the blood glucose at that stage is fairly high at 15.1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So moving back, please, and on to tile 10, do we see, no doubt we'll hear probably as a consequence of that, Actrapid, which is a type of insulin, was started on [Baby F] at 03.40 hours in the early hours of Friday, 31 July?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And we see that 1 hour and 1 minute later, [Baby F]'s blood glucose level had come down to 8.7?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, that's recorded by Ailsa Simpson on that same form that we saw just a few moments ago?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. The next entry is at 6.20, which is a record of the fact that the insulin was stopped for [Baby F].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And that is the relevant records for Friday the 31st; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tile 13 moves us on to the Saturday, 1 August. We see that at the handover that evening, so the Saturday into the Sunday, Lucy Letby came on shift; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: If we go to the information behind the tile, please, we see that for that night shift, the 1st into 2 August, Lucy Letby was the designated nurse for [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: The next tile, tile 14, is the following day, but just over midnight. So the same night shift and Lucy Letby still [Baby F]'s designated nurse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And this is a total parenteral nutrition prescription chart, which records the fact that lipid was finished; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's at 00.20 hours that morning.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Moving on to tile 15, please. Do we see that a new set of lipids was started at the time that the previous prescription was finished?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So this is part of the feeding regime for [Baby F], wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Just to remind the jury, I think we've heard from various witnesses that lipids are given when babies are not receiving milk.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We come next, at tile 16, to the night shift the following night. Of course, this is the shift on which [Baby E] died. We see that Lucy Letby again was on duty and she was again the designated nurse for [Baby F] --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- and [Baby E], as we've heard previously.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: As before, on the next tile, tile 17, do we have the chart for the parenteral nutrition fluid?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can we go to it this time, please, and go to the actual -- thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So what we see here, Mrs Hocknell, is not only the entry for this particular evening but also the previous entries; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So we'll hear a lot more detail about this during the evidence, but day 4 of [Baby E]'s life, we see at the top, being 1 August.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We see if we go across, we can see the amount that was to be given daily, that figure divided by 24 to give us the hourly rate at 8.06, the route intravenous, and Dr Ventress, the prescribing doctor, that it was started at just after midnight, so just coming into 2 August; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That this was a continuing bag?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We see Lucy Letby's signature below that from the previous night's shift, the one we've just looked at, and that this bag, in other words the day 4 bag, was due to finish at 00.10 on 3 August?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's the lipids time, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So we have both the Babiven and the lipid prescription ending at that time. We see the start in the block below, don't we, the day 5 block?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So we see it starting at 00.10 hours on the 3rd?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we go back to the sequence, please. So that's tile 17.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 18 shows us that on the night shift, the 3rd into 4 August, Lucy Letby was again the designated nurse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: This shows the events concerning [Baby E] as black tiles at tiles 19 and 20.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 21, do we have the nursing notes written by Belinda Simcock at 5.58?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We will be hearing from Belinda Simcock, but if we just click behind this tile, please, do we see that Belinda Simcock records sharing the care of [Baby F] due to the resuscitation and collapse of [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Going back to tiles, please, do you then record at tile 22 the fact that the records that follow this stage are in effect a detailed account for [Baby F]'s care from 01.00 hours on 4 August?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. So moving on to that material then, please, do we have what we're now familiar with, the collection of observation and intensive care charts on the hour, every hour?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, at 1 am.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So starting at 1 am. If we just look at this one, please. I'm not going to come back to the detail every time with these charts. The jury have had then explained many times in the context of different children. But do we see there the trace of the heart rate, respiratory rate and temperatures recorded for [Baby F] between 18.00 hours on 3 August 2015 and 17.00 hours on 4 August?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. If we can come out of that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Move next to tile 24, which is the intensive care fluid balance charts, and go to the document again. So again, these are charts or this is a chart which we will examine in detail with the witnesses concerned, but as before, do they record the similar or the same types of data that we have seen in previous cases --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: -- over a 24-hour period?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. So coming out of that again, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The third of the charts on the hour is the intensive care chart and environmental safety check. If we can do the same exercise for this. I think this is the other half of the chart, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's the same chart but this record is for the lefthand side of that chart --
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- whereas the previous one was for the right-hand side.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Okay. Thank you. We're not going to do this every time, but it's just to put us back into the way of thinking of how the documents work.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that's 1 am. If we return to the timeline, do we see there at tile 26 a record of -- or a marker for the death of [Baby E] at 01.40?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then at 2 o'clock, do we see Belinda Simcock making a record on the charts that we've just been looking at?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On one of the charts, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And at 2.30, the other two charts have the relevant records recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Tiles 28 and 29, that's at 02.30.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do we then see at 03.30, the same three charts being marked up with data?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's tiles 30 through to 32.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At 4 o'clock and at 4.30, between tiles 33 and 35, do we see the same three charts being marked up with the record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And that is replicated again at 05.30 between tiles 36 and 38?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Moving on to tile 39, please, do we have the nursing update made on the computer by Belinda Simcock?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, she will come to give evidence, so we will deal with those notes with her.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As we've seen on other occasions with other children, do we see at about the same time a note made on the computerised nursing record relating to communications with the [Babies E & F] family?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: That's tile 40. Do we then move on to, at tile 41, the fact that [Baby F] was given some supplemental oxygen?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Prescribed some supplemental oxygen, I should say.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then at tiles 42 through to 44, do we see at 06.30 the same three charts being marked up with the data observed at that time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Then just at about handover time, tiles 45 through to 47, do we again see the same three charts being recorded, being marked up, I should say?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 48, next, please, do we have the handover on the morning of 4 August from Belinda Simcock/Lucy Letby to [Nurse B]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, [Nurse B] will be giving evidence so I'm not going to ask you to deal with those notes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we move then to tiles 49 to 51? Do we see the same three records being marked up on the hour at 8 o'clock?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: There then follow three tiles, 52 through to 54, and we'll deal with these, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: 52, could we go to -- there's no name recorded on this, but these are some lab results which include blood test results, I think. Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can we just look at the original document, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So we see that in fact this is a chart which starts with the record made on 29 July, ends with the record made on 11 August, but the record that we are dealing with is the one on 4 August, which is three in from the right and is a reasonably full list of various levels, which notably, in the context of this case, does not include a glucose level, I think.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: I say notably in the context of this case because this case is about insulin, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: All right. Can we return back to the carousel, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is there particular reason why that chart has been put in at that point given that it doesn't have a time recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On the tile 51, it's listed major events as "weekly bloods".
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So in the context of what was available, this was the record that matched that.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Okay. So tile 51, I won't ask us to go back to it, but that's [Nurse B]'s notes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Which suggest that that's when the bloods were taken?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So the next tile at 52, that's why you've put in the results there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At tile 53 do we have [Nurse B]'s notes, which she can deal with?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: As also appear at tile 54?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: For the sake of the narrative, do the notes at tile 54 record the fact that at the beginning of the shift she was making the usual equipment checks that we have seen in many other cases?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And a general observation or general observations concerning the care of [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. At tile 55 -- and we'll go to this one, please -- is this a blood gas record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, at 8.16.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: This does include a glucose reading, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we highlight that, please, so we have the context.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is 8.16 on 4 August, please. Towards the bottom.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's just above the bottom of the screen.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do we see recorded there a glucose level of 3.8, which is where the arrow is now?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: We've heard that that's in the normal range.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's what I understand, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So glucose omitted from the lab sample from a sample taken at about this time, but included in the blood gas sample taken between 8 and 9 am?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can we go back to the carousel, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 56. Does that record the receipt of the sample, of the blood sample that is, at the lab at 08.38?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So is that the sample, the results of which are recorded at tile 52?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Do we move next, please, to the usual trio of charts that we have seen on the hour or on the half hour every hour?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: So that's tiles 57 through to 59?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, these are all annotated by [Nurse B], so we'll ask her to deal with the details.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do we come next to some prescriptions at 09.17 from tile 60 through to tile 63?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: They record the prescription of sodium chloride, caffeine, benzylpenicillin and sucrose?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At 10 o'clock, from tile 64 through to tile 66, again do we have the three sets of readings recorded?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And again, two were recorded by Shelley Tomlins, the fluid requirement chart recorded by [Nurse B]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Thank you. Do we come next, at tile 67, to some notes made by Dr Beech?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Can we go just to your summary, please, because Dr Beech will be giving evidence, but just to keep the jury apprised of what's going on.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Does this -- without going into the details, does this go into quite some detail about various readings that had been reported to Dr Beech by that stage?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. This is the weekly NNU review, so this is why it might go into a bit more detail.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Do we see on the fifth line of your typed summary:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Hyper [that is high] glycaemia [blood sugar] resolved"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And we then see various measurements for [Baby E], the fact he was on Optiflow, the fact that he was on the 9th to the 25th centile.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: His weight, the fact that he was active and the fact that he was going to be scanned, immunisations not yet done, and the management plan to wean him off Optiflow?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At the bottom I think there's observations made by Dr Beech, but again we'll let her deal with those if we may. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So moving back to the carousel, please. Between tiles 68 and 70, do we have the usual three charts filled in with data by the designated nurse?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, for 11 am.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And we have exactly the same types of data for 12 o'clock at tiles 71 to 73?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: At tile 74, do we see that [Baby F] was prescribed nystatin?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: And at tiles 75 to 77, do we see the same three charts as we have seen on the hour, up to this stage, every hour, at this time one with a record at 13.00 and the other two with records at 13.15?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HOCKNELL

blocks.text: Again, we'll let the relevant witnesses or witness in this case deal with those.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do we have a further record of the same heads of data at 14.00 hours between tiles 78 and 80?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON
